To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we could show the non-Markowian character of the spontaneous emission dynamics in a photonic crystal by ferromagnetic resonances in the YIG spheres.
the radiation-induced linewidth of a magnetic dipolar emitter is strongly suppressed inside the photonic band gap of a woodpile structure.

the radiation dynamics of a ferromagnetic resonance in the photonic crystal is strongly modified compared to free space, and that the spontaneous emission rate is strongly modified inside the photonic band gap.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the investigation of spontaneous emission control in a magnetic system.
the development of novel materials and devices for future photonic and optoelectronic applications.
the interaction between light and matter in photonic crystals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the radiation dynamics of a point-like magnetic emitter is governed by a non-Markov master equation.
the radiation dynamics of a single crystal YIG sphere fixed inside a photonic alumina woodpile crystal has been experimentally realized as an analogue for a point-like emitter inside such a crystal.
the spontaneous radiation of a magnetic dipol in a photonic crystal can be completely controlled by the photonic crystal.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we were able to show that spontaneous emission control can be achieved by using photonic crystals.
we could show for the first time that the photonic band gap effect can be used for the control of the spontaneous emission of a magnetic dipolar source.
the spontaneous emission rate of an optical emitter can be controlled by placing it in a photonic band gap material.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the radiation feedback of an emitter can be controlled in a wide range by a suitable choice of the dielectric environment.
the photonic crystal is a very promising candidate for the realization of optical devices that are based on a controlled spontaneous emission process.
the photonic crystals can be designed in such a manner that the spontaneous emission can be suppressed or enhanced.
